title: test: mention-provenance.ps1 fails its child-host probe whenever its parent is Windows PowerShell 5.1
description:
Found while planning task-86431c315e524b3b89af3bb3d2e7c98d (2026-11-02). It is a pre-existing harness bug, unrelated to that row's seam.

Repro, at HEAD 7aa4148c, from a clean export of the tree on D: (no task worktree involved):
`powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts\tests\mention-provenance.ps1 -PowerShell powershell`
It exits 1 before any wrapper launch:
`FAIL: child host probe failed (exit 1); the stored-timestamp guard cannot be trusted on powershell`
The child prints `PROBE_HOST : The term 'PROBE_HOST' is not recognized ... CommandNotFoundException`.

Cause: the probe runs `& $psExe -NoProfile -Command $probeScript` (scripts/tests/mention-provenance.ps1, around line 62). Windows PowerShell 5.1's legacy native-argument passing drops the double quotes embedded in $probeScript, so the child runs `PROBE_HOST exe= + ...` as a command instead of a string.

The same file PASSES under a PowerShell 7 parent, `pwsh.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts\tests\mention-provenance.ps1`, with both `-PowerShell powershell` and `-PowerShell pwsh`. The default pwsh child under a 5.1 parent goes through the same 5.1 argument path, so expect it to fail too.

Logs: D:\moe-scratch\t86431\ps\s1-mp.log (5.1 parent, FAIL) and s1-mp7-51.log / s1-mp7.log (pwsh parent, PASSED).

Fix direction, verify before use: pass the probe as -EncodedCommand (base64 of the UTF-16LE script), which both engines accept and no native quoting can damage. Keep the probe's purpose: a child that cannot answer must still fail the harness.
definitionOfDone: Under a Windows PowerShell 5.1 parent, `powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts\tests\mention-provenance.ps1` prints `mention-provenance.ps1 PASSED` with `-PowerShell powershell` and with `-PowerShell pwsh`.
Under a pwsh parent, the same two runs still print PASSED.
A child that cannot answer the probe still fails the harness with exit 1 and the `child host probe failed` line, for example `-PowerShell` naming a nonexistent exe.
The probe still records the PROBE_HOST and PROBE_TYPES lines it prints today; only the transport of the script to the child changes.
The new or changed lines are ASCII only, because the file has no BOM and PowerShell 5.1 reads it as ANSI.
